Read a Python value

Source: R/guest.R
py_value.Rd

py_value() reads a value that a Python chunk made, in R code, and checks it as weft checks every value that reaches prose (rules 1.11 and 2.12.4). Each argument is one string, a step of a path: py_value("n") reads the name n in Python's main module; py_value("cfg", "depth") reads cfg, then its key depth when cfg is a mapping, else its attribute depth.

Usage

py_value(...)

Arguments

...

One or more non-empty strings: the name in Python's main module, then the keys or attributes below it.

Value

The R form of the value: a logical, integer or double, a character string, a Date, or an atomic vector of one of these for a list, named when it was a mapping. A missing value is NA.

Details

The value is read from its Python type, never from reticulate's conversion, which turns a whole number beyond 2^31 into NA or a wrong number. A bool, an integer, a float, a decimal.Decimal, a string, a datetime.date and a list of one of these (a list, a tuple, a mapping with string keys, a one-dimensional numpy array or a pandas Series) are read. An integer beyond 2^53, a Decimal of more than 15 significant digits, a datetime, a set and anything else are refused with a weft_guest_value_error that says what to do. None, NaN and infinities are NA.

In prose, in the expressions weft evaluates, py$n and py[["n"]] are read the same way, with no library(reticulate). Use py_value() in the code of an R chunk.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) &&
    isTRUE(tryCatch(reticulate::py_available(initialize = TRUE),
                    error = function(e) FALSE))) {
  reticulate::py_run_string("depth = 3.14159")
  py_value("depth")
}
#> Downloading uv...
#> Done!
#> [1] 3.14159
